main_issue: Whether and how Agent D can keep cooking strong-smelling devil curry given the smell affecting A, B and C, and what arrangement (timing, notice, avoiding laundry days) resolves it.

A-B.evidence: Both complain about the smell (T1, T2); B says the after-7 timing A proposed doesn't help (T8), but B accepts D's notice arrangement (T16). They never directly clash.

A-C.evidence: Both complain about the smell (T1, T3). C says the after-7 timing doesn't help (T9). C ends with the laundry-day avoidance (T23), and A is silent on it.

A-D.evidence: A asks D to cook after 7 or at weekends (T5). D agrees (T6). A thanks D (T7). D later adds notice and laundry-day avoidance (T13, T27), and A says nothing against these.

B-C.evidence: B says 'the smell still comes into my room' (T8). C replies 'Same for me' (T9). They end with different fixes: B accepts notice (T16), C wants laundry days avoided (T23).

B-D.evidence: D asks B about timing (T10). B asks for notice (T12). D agrees (T13). B says 'that works for me' (T16).

C-D.evidence: C rejects notice (T14) and moving the laundry (T18, T21). D offers to avoid Mon/Wed/Fri (T22). C requests it (T23) and D agrees (T27).
